data.description:
## Description

**What**: Disappeared-from-Jira classifier in differ + inbound_probe applier leaf. Routes missing issues to {hard-delete, trash-and-restore, project-move, out-of-window} via a single REST GET per missing issue.
**Why**: The four-branch fork is the only safe way to distinguish hard-delete from project-move or out-of-window update; without it, a stale label sweep could destroy a legitimate ticket.
**Scope**:
- IN: differ probe emission, inbound_probe leaf (REST GET only), 4-branch classification, follow-on mutation emission
- OUT: Webhook-driven invalidation, eager re-creation

## Done Definitions

- Given a local ticket with jira-* id whose Jira partner is missing from the fetchers working set, the differ emits an (inbound, probe) mutation; a unit test exercises this on a fixture with one absent and one present partner ← Satisfies: sc-4
- The inbound_probe leaf classifies four branches against per-branch throwaway DIG issue fixtures: hard-delete (404 with no project), trash-and-restore (410 with restore-trail), project-move (200 with project.key != DIG), out-of-window (200 within DIG but updated older than fetcher window) — one fixture-driven test per branch ← Satisfies: sc-4
- An inbound_probe invocation performs zero write calls against Jira (only a REST GET); a test asserts the call envelope is GET-only ← Satisfies: sc-4, sc-1
- Unit tests written and passing for all new logic ← Validates Closure Check: "TDD DoD"

## Considerations

- [Security] The probe REST GET is read-only by contract; any future change that adds a write must trip a CI guard.
- [Reliability] Each of the four branches must be exercised against a throwaway DIG issue at integration time.

## Escalation Policy

**Escalation policy**: Proceed unless a significant assumption is required to continue — one that could send the implementation in the wrong direction. Escalate only when genuinely blocked without a reasonable inference. Document all assumptions made without escalating.
data.title: As a reconciler operator, I want a disappeared-from-Jira classifier that routes via inbound_probe REST GET
